questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Going to a big city with plenty of opportunities, subcultures and exploring the capital and the lifestyle here.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: What made my stay was the people I've met and the things if been doing in my freetime more than my experience with the university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult, I spent many many hours on trying to figure out the website of Sorbonne, trying to find which courses were available to me etc. I had to be in close contact with my councelors in order to solve administrative challenges and the host university was impossible to reach.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was still in contact with the studyabroad councelors from Denmark online, but I didn't receive any assistance in Paris.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was very complicated to figure out who to contact for various problems, and the administrators from Sorbonne kept telling me to contact someone else, as if no one knew who was actually supposed to help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky and found housing through the only person I knew in Paris before. I recommend making an instagram-story, even if you don't feel like you have contacts - you might still know someone who knows someone! Also I don't recommend searching through facebook groups, it seems like everything on there are scams even if it seems ligit (with agencies, reliable profiles, pictures of ID and official documents it can still be a scam). If you are still searching through facebook it is a necessecity to see the place in real life before signing or paying anything! So I recommend going to Paris for some time and visitting places - if they end up not being able to show you or keep re-scheduling the visit, you can't trust them.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid of living in the suburbs, that's where the Parisians live and where you can find cheaper housing and live with other people! Many of the suburbs are still very lively and cultural. Living in the city center is expensive and you'll most likely find a tiny studio for a high price. But if you go a bit further out, you'll find very nice housing with other people for a reasonable price - and you might even get the possibility to get to know French people and not only foreigners.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There were a lot of steps and deadlines, so you have to check your ku-mail often. Some of the steps take a long time and are quite frustrating, especially the pre-approval that is difficult to make and feels meaningless since you'll most likely get completely different courses when you arrive. We had a nice introduction to everything and the councelors were always helpfull and fast at answering.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The UCPHabroad councelors, the student councelors and studienævnet.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty succesfull, but it was all a gamble and I was lucky with showing up in good time and having professors that accepted me even though there weren't officially more spots in the classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The registration process is chaotic, tou show up and write what classes you want on a paper - and then you get a spot if there are still available spots, if not you have to find another class. I recommend already making the puzzle with plan B's before the day where you sign up and showing up in good time so the popular spots aren't already filled.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two courses on the 3rd year, and they were the most interesting but very difficult! The courses on 1st and 2nd year were easier but felt a lot like high school classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very authoritorian. The teachers were mostly talking and always presented the right answer. Even if they facilitated a dialogue with the students they would present their own "right" interpretation afterwards. The teachers would be direct with interrupting the students and letting them know if they didn't agree with their answers.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Littératures francophones if you have a good level of French - same with litteraturen européenes. I would also recommend the SIAL/FLE course.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is expensive + public transportation. Cultural offers are not very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything you can imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try some of the sport offers.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around France if you have the time. Go to the south with the train network! Enjoy the many museums of Paris if you enjoy that. Go to koncerts and events. Engage in local politics and activism. Markets, independant cinemas, cycle around the city, go to the forest and see the different suburbs.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I was engaged in a very local group of French people that were extremely open and introduced me to their friends and lives. Of course it was difficult not speaking French fluently and not knowing anyone before, but they were very welcoming and people I'm staying in contact with!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I actually didn't really socialize with the local students since I had such a big network connected to the people I lived with. But I do recommend socializing through dating apps, also if it's just to find friends. In that way you can find people you align with and whom are also interested in new connections.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Discussing and complaining a lot. I found it difficult to participate in those kinds of conversations.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way of welcoming me, bringing me with them and introducing me to their friends and social groups. The way of having a home that was always open for and curious towards guests and how they tried to include me in their conversations even with my level of French.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Live with other people, it will open up tour world and give you connections to the city that you can keep afterwards. Come some time before and/or stay after, so you have time to explore the city and travel. Reach out to other erasmus students and to the local students to get through the courses.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't let it tear you down that you're not doing well in the classes. Be curious and ask questions. Find other erasmus students in your classes and help each other. Focus on the formalia of the exams, it counts a lot, even more than the content.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know all of these people and improving my French. Getting to know a new city and having connections here now, that I can come back to. Learning more about French culture and politics. Experiencing the French school system even though I don't see myself thriving in it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Passing the exams and cracking the code of how to write them. Even just understanding and following the courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: The university will be tough, so try to put yourself in to other constelations that bring you joy while you're here - and that will make it more than worth it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
